intro: Hi! At B1 you learnt partners for make, do, say, tell, have, take and get. Now we go further: adjectives with nouns (heavy traffic), verbs with nouns at work (meet a deadline) and adverbs with adjectives (highly unlikely), so your English sounds natural, not translated. Warm-up: how do you say 'jalanan macet' in English?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line from b1-collocations-basic (don't re-teach it): collocations (kolokasi) = words that usually go together, learnt as chunks (make a mistake, do homework, tell me, take a photo, take medicine). This lesson adds three new kinds: adjective + noun, verb + noun (work), adverb + adjective. Explain the terms plainly the first time: adjective = kata sifat (describes a noun: heavy, strong), noun = kata benda (traffic, coffee), verb = kata kerja (meet, raise), adverb = here a word that makes an adjective stronger, like very (highly, fully, deeply). The key message: the wrong partner isn't 'wrong grammar', it just sounds unnatural or translated, so learn the PAIR, not the single word, and write new words down with their partner (not 'deadline' but 'meet a deadline'). Dictionary tip: a collocation dictionary (the Oxford Collocations Dictionary; free sites such as Ozdic) or the example sentences in a learner's dictionary (Cambridge, Oxford Learner's) show which partners are normal. Ozdic's current word pages are sometimes incomplete (its 'traffic' page didn't list heavy when checked), so if a list looks odd, tell the learner to double-check in Cambridge Dictionary.

Adjective + noun. heavy = a lot of: heavy traffic (lalu lintas padat / macet), heavy rain (hujan deras), heavy snow. strong = powerful or concentrated: strong coffee / tea (kental, kuat; opposite weak coffee), a strong accent (logat kental; a thick or heavy accent is also correct, so never test accent against thick/heavy), a strong wind (not heavy wind). Prices are high or low (harga mahal / murah): the price is high, rice is expensive; *'the price is expensive' copies harga mahal; teach 'a low price' (a 'cheap price' is heard informally: don't test it). a tight deadline (tenggat mepet; not *narrow deadline; 'a hard deadline' is a different, real term = a fixed deadline that can't move: don't use it as a distractor). a serious problem (masalah serius / berat; big and major problem are also correct; *heavy problem copies masalah berat). a major decision (keputusan besar; a big decision is also correct); keputusan berat = a difficult / tough / hard decision, not *heavy decision. The node's common error: *'The traffic is very crowded today' → heavy (or bad). crowded = full of PEOPLE: a crowded train, a crowded market; busy = a busy road / street. macet = there's a traffic jam / the traffic is heavy.

Verb + noun at work. meet a deadline (selesai tepat waktu, memenuhi tenggat) / miss a deadline; the node's common error *'We have to reach the deadline' → meet. reach / achieve a goal or a target is correct (so: reach a goal, but meet a deadline); 'meet a target' is also correct; 'make the deadline' is informal but correct: accept it. raise an issue / a question / a concern (menyampaikan, mengangkat masalah); 'bring up an issue' is the same (phrasal verb): accept it. Learners confuse raise (needs an object: raise an issue, raise prices) with rise (no object: prices rise). hold a meeting (mengadakan rapat, a bit formal); have a meeting is everyday and also correct, so never test hold against have; attend a meeting = hadir. set a goal / a target (menetapkan target; not *put a goal from 'pasang target'). make progress (ada kemajuan): uncountable, so not *a progress / *progresses, and not *do progress. take responsibility for (bertanggung jawab atas); accept responsibility is also correct. run a business / a company / a shop (menjalankan usaha); own / start a business are also correct; 'do business' (B1) is a different chunk = berbisnis. pay attention to (memperhatikan; not *give attention / *make attention).

Adverb + adjective. Indonesian uses sangat / sungguh for everything; in English very, really and extremely are safe with most normal adjectives (very unlikely, very different, very disappointed), but natural English often picks a partner: highly + likely / unlikely, recommended, successful, qualified; fully + aware (100%), booked, charged; deeply + feelings: concerned (prihatin, khawatir), moved, sorry; completely / totally + different, wrong, impossible; bitterly + disappointed (also bitterly cold, more British). The node's common error *'It's strongly unlikely' → highly unlikely: strongly goes with verbs of opinion (strongly agree, disagree, believe, recommend, advise). Near-equivalents that are ALL correct, so never test them against each other: very / highly / extremely unlikely; fully / well / very aware; deeply / bitterly / very disappointed; completely / totally / entirely / quite / very different; deeply / very / seriously concerned; highly / strongly recommended (in instructions 'It is strongly recommended' is normal; 'I highly recommend it' is also common). Only test pairs where the other options are clearly unnatural (*heavily aware, *strongly unlikely, *highly different, *fully disappointed). With 'absolute' adjectives (impossible, perfect) use completely / totally / absolutely, not very: mention only if asked.

At B2 collocations are tendencies, not laws: accept any natural alternative and say which one is most common. Grammar limits: A0–B1 grammar only (present / past simple and continuous, present perfect, future forms, first and second conditional, modals, present / past simple passive like 'is highly recommended', reported statements, defining relative clauses, gerunds / infinitives). No third conditional, wish, past modals, participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses or advanced passive. Don't add more collocation families (C1 sets like 'fierce competition', 'bear responsibility') or idioms unless the learner asks; phrasal verbs only as alternatives (bring up). Contexts: Jakarta / Bandung / Surabaya offices and startups, KRL / MRT, ojek online, rainy-season floods, prices in rupiah. Correct one thing at a time, usually a word-by-word partner from Indonesian (crowded traffic, strong rain, thick coffee, expensive price, heavy problem, reach the deadline, strongly unlikely).

keyPoints.title: Adjective + noun
keyPoints.explanation: Some adjectives (words that describe a noun) have fixed partners. heavy = a lot of: heavy traffic (not crowded traffic: crowded is for places full of people), heavy rain (not strong rain). strong = powerful: strong coffee (not thick coffee), a strong accent, a strong wind. Prices are high or low (not 'expensive price'); a deadline with little time is tight. Indonesian berat isn't always heavy: masalah berat = a serious problem, keputusan besar = a major decision.

examples.en: There's heavy traffic on the toll road to Bandung.
This coffee is too strong for me.
examples.id: Kopi ini terlalu kental buat saya.

examples.en: Losing our biggest client is a serious problem.
examples.id: Kehilangan klien terbesar kita adalah masalah serius.

id.title: Kata sifat + kata benda
id.explanation: Beberapa kata sifat (kata yang menjelaskan kata benda) punya pasangan tetap. heavy = banyak, padat: heavy traffic (macet; bukan crowded traffic, karena crowded untuk tempat yang penuh orang), heavy rain (hujan deras; bukan strong rain). strong = kuat: strong coffee (kopi kental; bukan thick coffee), a strong accent (logat kental), a strong wind (angin kencang). Harga itu high atau low (bukan 'expensive price'); tenggat yang mepet itu tight. Berat tidak selalu heavy: masalah berat = a serious problem, keputusan besar = a major decision.

keyPoints.title: Verb + noun at work
keyPoints.explanation: At work, many nouns have their own verb: meet a deadline (not reach the deadline: you reach a goal), miss a deadline, raise an issue (bring it up at a meeting), hold a meeting, set a goal, make progress (not do progress), take responsibility for something, run a business, pay attention to something. Learn the verb and the noun together.

examples.en: If we work on Saturday, we can still meet the deadline.
examples.id: Kalau kita kerja hari Sabtu, kita masih bisa selesai tepat waktu.

examples.en: Sari raised an important question at the meeting.
examples.id: Sari menyampaikan pertanyaan penting di rapat.

examples.en: Bu Ani runs a small catering business in Surabaya.
examples.id: Bu Ani menjalankan usaha katering kecil di Surabaya.

id.title: Kata kerja + kata benda di dunia kerja
id.explanation: Di kantor, banyak kata benda punya kata kerjanya sendiri: meet a deadline (memenuhi tenggat; bukan reach the deadline, karena reach untuk target: reach a goal), miss a deadline (melewati tenggat), raise an issue (menyampaikan masalah di rapat), hold a meeting (mengadakan rapat), set a goal (menetapkan target), make progress (ada kemajuan; bukan do progress), take responsibility for (bertanggung jawab atas), run a business (menjalankan usaha), pay attention to (memperhatikan). Hafalkan kata kerja dan kata bendanya bersama-sama.

keyPoints.title: Adverb + adjective
keyPoints.explanation: very is always safe, but natural English often uses a partner adverb to make an adjective stronger: highly unlikely, highly recommended, highly successful; fully aware; deeply concerned; completely different; bitterly disappointed. Not 'strongly unlikely': strongly goes with verbs of opinion (I strongly agree, I strongly believe).

examples.en: It's highly unlikely that the office will close early today.
examples.id: Kecil sekali kemungkinannya kantor tutup lebih awal hari ini.

examples.en: Life in Jakarta is completely different from life in my village.
examples.id: Hidup di Jakarta sama sekali berbeda dengan hidup di desa saya.

examples.en: Dimas was bitterly disappointed with his test result.
examples.id: Dimas sangat kecewa dengan hasil tesnya.

id.title: Adverb + kata sifat
id.explanation: very selalu aman, tapi bahasa Inggris yang alami sering memakai adverb (kata keterangan yang menguatkan kata sifat) pasangan tertentu: highly unlikely (kecil sekali kemungkinannya), highly recommended (sangat direkomendasikan), highly successful (sangat sukses); fully aware (sadar sepenuhnya); deeply concerned (sangat prihatin); completely different (sama sekali berbeda); bitterly disappointed (sangat kecewa). Bukan 'strongly unlikely': strongly berpasangan dengan kata kerja pendapat (I strongly agree, I strongly believe).

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one adjective (kopi kental): Pak Hasan always orders a very ___ coffee before a long meeting.
expected: strong
guidedPractice.hint: kental here doesn't mean thick: coffee with a lot of taste is strong coffee (the opposite is weak coffee).

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one adjective (keputusan besar): Moving to Singapore for work was a ___ decision for Dimas.
expected: major
big
guidedPractice.hint: An important decision that changes a lot is a major decision (or a big decision). Not 'heavy decision'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb (menetapkan target): At the start of each year, our manager ___ clear goals for the whole team.
expected: sets
set
guidedPractice.hint: The partner of goal is set: set a goal. Not 'put a goal' (from pasang target). Our manager = he or she, so sets.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb (menjalankan usaha): Bu Ani ___ a small catering business from her home in Bandung.
expected: runs
is running
guidedPractice.hint: To manage a business is to run it: run a business. Bu Ani = she, so runs.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which adverb fits best: highly, bitterly or fully? The new Padang restaurant near our office is ___ recommended on food apps.
expected: highly
guidedPractice.hint: highly goes with words that judge something as good or likely: highly recommended, highly successful.

independentPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: My boss gave us a very narrow deadline for the report.
expected: my boss gave us a very tight deadline for the report
my boss gave us a tight deadline for the report
independentPractice.hint: A deadline with very little time (mepet) is tight, not narrow.

independentPractice.prompt: Write in English: Kita perlu mengadakan rapat dengan tim IT minggu depan.
expected: we need to hold a meeting with the it team next week
we need to have a meeting with the it team next week
we have to hold a meeting with the it team next week
we have to have a meeting with the it team next week
we need to hold a meeting with the it team next week please
next week we need to hold a meeting with the it team
next week we need to have a meeting with the it team
independentPractice.hint: mengadakan rapat = hold a meeting (a bit formal) or have a meeting (everyday). Not 'make a meeting'.

independentPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Pak Hasan runs a heavily successful logistics company in Surabaya.
expected: pak hasan runs a highly successful logistics company in surabaya
pak hasan runs a very successful logistics company in surabaya
pak hasan runs an extremely successful logistics company in surabaya
pak hasan runs a hugely successful logistics company in surabaya
independentPractice.hint: heavily doesn't go with successful. The usual partner is highly (or very).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake (keep 'The traffic' as the start): The traffic on Jalan Sudirman is very crowded this morning.
acceptableAnswers: the traffic on jalan sudirman is very heavy this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is very bad this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is really heavy this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is really bad this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is heavy this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is extremely heavy this morning
the traffic on jalan sudirman is terrible this morning
assessment.rubric: Correct: The traffic on Jalan Sudirman is very heavy this morning (heavy traffic = lalu lintas padat / macet). 'very bad' = 100 (also natural). 'Jalan Sudirman is very busy / crowded this morning' = 70 (natural, but the task said to keep 'The traffic'). 'The traffic is very jammed' = 40. 'very busy traffic' = 50 (understood, but heavy is the usual partner). Unchanged 'crowded' = 0 (crowded is for places full of people).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: The price of rice in Surabaya is very expensive this month.
acceptableAnswers: the price of rice in surabaya is very high this month
the price of rice in surabaya is really high this month
the price of rice in surabaya is high this month
rice in surabaya is very expensive this month
rice is very expensive in surabaya this month
the price of rice in surabaya is extremely high this month
rice in surabaya is really expensive this month
assessment.rubric: Correct: The price of rice in Surabaya is very high this month (a price is high or low; things are expensive or cheap). 'Rice in Surabaya is very expensive this month' = 100 (the thing is expensive). 'The price … is very big' = 30. 'The price … is very costly' = 30. Unchanged 'the price is expensive' = 0 (copies harga mahal).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: We worked all weekend, so we reached the deadline.
acceptableAnswers: we worked all weekend so we met the deadline
we worked all weekend so we were able to meet the deadline
we worked all weekend so we managed to meet the deadline
we worked all weekend so we could meet the deadline
we worked all weekend so we made the deadline
assessment.rubric: Correct: We worked all weekend, so we met the deadline (meet a deadline = selesai tepat waktu; met is the past). 'managed to meet / were able to meet' = 100. 'made the deadline' = 100 (informal but correct). 'so we meet the deadline' = 60 (right partner, wrong tense). 'achieved / caught the deadline' = 10. Unchanged 'reached' = 0 (you reach a goal, not a deadline).

assessment.prompt: Write the verb that means 'menyampaikan / mengangkat', in the correct form: At yesterday's meeting, Sari ___ an important issue about the new working hours.
acceptableAnswers: raised
brought up
assessment.rubric: Correct: raised (raise an issue = menyampaikan masalah; yesterday = past simple). 'brought up' = 100 (phrasal verb with the same meaning). 'raise' or 'raises' = 50 (right verb, wrong tense). 'rose' or 'rised' = 30 (rise has no object: prices rise). 'mentioned' = 70 (natural, but not the collocation asked for). 'lifted' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one verb: Please ___ close attention to the safety instructions on the next slide.
acceptableAnswers: pay
assessment.rubric: Correct: pay (pay attention to = memperhatikan; pay close attention = memperhatikan baik-baik). 'give' = 30 (understood, but not the usual partner). 'make', 'do' or 'put' = 0. 'paying' or 'paid' = 50 (right verb, wrong form after Please).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: It's strongly unlikely that Pak Hasan will change his mind.
acceptableAnswers: it's highly unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it is highly unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
its highly unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it's very unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it is very unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it's extremely unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it is extremely unlikely that pak hasan will change his mind
it's highly unlikely pak hasan will change his mind
it is highly unlikely pak hasan will change his mind
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's highly unlikely that Pak Hasan will change his mind (highly unlikely = kecil sekali kemungkinannya). 'very / extremely unlikely' = 100 (also natural; highly is the typical partner). 'deeply / heavily unlikely' = 10. Removing the adverb ('It's unlikely …') = 50 (grammatical but avoids the collocation). Unchanged 'strongly unlikely' = 0 (strongly goes with verbs of opinion: strongly agree).

assessment.prompt: Complete with fully, bitterly or heavily: Before you sign the contract, make sure you are ___ aware of all the costs.
acceptableAnswers: fully
assessment.rubric: Correct: fully (fully aware = sadar sepenuhnya, 100% aware). 'well' or 'completely' = 80 (natural, but not one of the three choices). 'bitterly' = 0 (it goes with disappointed). 'heavily' = 0.

material.title: Learn the pair, not the word

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: **collocations** are words that usually go together, like **make a mistake**, **tell the truth** and **take a photo**. You learnt them as **chunks** (one piece, like one long word).

At B2 your grammar is good, so the next step to sounding natural is choosing the **right partner** for a word. In this lesson you'll learn three new kinds:
- **adjective + noun**: an **adjective** describes a **noun** (a thing): *heavy traffic, strong coffee*.
- **verb + noun**, especially at work: *meet a deadline, raise an issue*.
- **adverb + adjective**: here an **adverb** is a word like *very* that makes an adjective stronger: *highly unlikely, fully aware*.

The wrong partner (*crowded traffic, reach the deadline, strongly unlikely*) isn't a grammar mistake, and people will understand you. It just sounds **translated**. That's why at B2 a collocation is often a **tendency**: sometimes two partners are both fine (*a big / major decision*), and you just need one natural choice.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: **kolokasi** (collocation) adalah kata-kata yang biasa dipakai bersama, seperti **make a mistake**, **tell the truth** dan **take a photo**. Kamu menghafalnya sebagai **paket** (satu kesatuan, seperti satu kata panjang).

Di B2 tata bahasamu sudah bagus, jadi langkah berikutnya supaya terdengar alami adalah memilih **pasangan yang tepat** untuk sebuah kata. Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar tiga jenis baru:
- **kata sifat + kata benda**: **kata sifat** (adjective) menjelaskan **kata benda** (noun, yaitu benda atau hal): *heavy traffic, strong coffee*.
- **kata kerja + kata benda**, terutama di dunia kerja: *meet a deadline, raise an issue*.
- **adverb + kata sifat**: di sini **adverb** (kata keterangan) adalah kata seperti *very* yang menguatkan kata sifat: *highly unlikely, fully aware*.

Pasangan yang salah (*crowded traffic, reach the deadline, strongly unlikely*) bukan kesalahan tata bahasa, dan orang tetap paham maksudmu. Hanya saja terdengar seperti **terjemahan**. Karena itu di B2 kolokasi sering berupa **kecenderungan**: kadang dua pasangan sama-sama benar (*a big / major decision*), dan kamu cukup memilih satu yang alami.

id.note: kata kerja + kata benda (bukan 'reach the deadline')

blocks.text:
The **learn-the-pair habit**: when you meet a new noun, write it down **with its partner**, not alone. Not *deadline = tenggat*, but **meet a deadline = memenuhi tenggat**; not *rain*, but **heavy rain**.

Not sure which partner is natural? Check a **collocation dictionary**: it lists the words that usually go with a noun (the *Oxford Collocations Dictionary*, or free websites such as **Ozdic**). A learner's dictionary like **Cambridge Dictionary** also shows partners in its example sentences. If a list looks strange, compare two sources.

id.text:
**Kebiasaan hafal pasangannya**: kalau ketemu kata benda baru, catat **bersama pasangannya**, jangan sendirian. Jangan cuma *deadline = tenggat*, tapi **meet a deadline = memenuhi tenggat**; jangan cuma *rain*, tapi **heavy rain** (hujan deras).

Tidak yakin pasangan mana yang alami? Cek **kamus kolokasi**: kamus ini mendaftar kata-kata yang biasa dipakai bersama sebuah kata benda (*Oxford Collocations Dictionary*, atau situs gratis seperti **Ozdic**). Kamus pelajar seperti **Cambridge Dictionary** juga menunjukkan pasangan kata di contoh-contoh kalimatnya. Kalau daftarnya terlihat aneh, bandingkan dua sumber.

blocks.prompt: Which is the most useful way to write a new word in your vocabulary notebook?
blocks.explain: Writing the word with its partner shows you how to use it. 'deadline' alone doesn't tell you which verb to use, and Indonesian word-by-word gives the wrong one ('reach the deadline').

id.prompt: Cara mana yang paling berguna untuk mencatat kata baru di buku kosakatamu?
id.explain: Mencatat kata bersama pasangannya menunjukkan cara memakainya. 'deadline' saja tidak memberi tahu kata kerja apa yang dipakai, dan terjemahan kata per kata menghasilkan yang salah ('reach the deadline').

material.title: Adjective + noun: heavy traffic, strong coffee

blocks.text:
Some adjectives have favourite nouns. Learn them in small groups:
- **heavy** = a lot of: **heavy traffic** (macet, padat), **heavy rain** (hujan deras).
- **strong** = powerful, a lot of taste or sound: **strong coffee** (kopi kental; the opposite is *weak coffee*), **a strong accent** (logat kental), **a strong wind** (angin kencang). Why strong wind but heavy rain? No logic: it's just the partner, so learn the pair.
- **high / low** + price: **a high price, low prices**. A *thing* is expensive or cheap (*Rice is expensive*), but a *price* is high or low (*The price of rice is high*).
- **a tight deadline** = very little time to finish (mepet).
- **a serious problem** (masalah serius / berat) and **a major decision** (keputusan besar). *a big problem* and *a big decision* are fine too.

id.text:
Beberapa kata sifat punya kata benda favorit. Hafalkan dalam kelompok kecil:
- **heavy** = banyak, padat: **heavy traffic** (macet, padat), **heavy rain** (hujan deras).
- **strong** = kuat, rasanya atau suaranya kuat: **strong coffee** (kopi kental; lawannya *weak coffee*), **a strong accent** (logat kental), **a strong wind** (angin kencang). Kenapa strong wind tapi heavy rain? Tidak ada logikanya: memang itu pasangannya, jadi hafalkan pasangannya.
- **high / low** + price: **a high price, low prices** (harga mahal, harga murah). *Barangnya* expensive atau cheap (*Rice is expensive*), tapi *harganya* high atau low (*The price of rice is high*).
- **a tight deadline** = tenggat yang mepet, waktunya sedikit sekali.
- **a serious problem** (masalah serius / berat) dan **a major decision** (keputusan besar). *a big problem* dan *a big decision* juga benar.

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps: translating the adjective word by word gives the wrong partner.
- *macet / ramai* → not `crowded traffic`. **crowded** = full of **people**: *a crowded train, a crowded market*. Traffic is **heavy** (or **bad**).
- *hujan deras* → not `strong rain`: **heavy rain**.
- *kopi kental* → not `thick coffee` (*thick* is for soup or a book): **strong coffee**.
- *harganya mahal* → not `the price is expensive`: **the price is high**.
- *masalah berat* → not `a heavy problem`: **a serious problem**. *keputusan berat* = **a difficult / tough decision**.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: menerjemahkan kata sifat kata per kata menghasilkan pasangan yang salah.
- *macet / ramai* → bukan `crowded traffic`. **crowded** = penuh **orang**: *a crowded train* (kereta yang penuh sesak), *a crowded market*. Lalu lintas itu **heavy** (atau **bad**).
- *hujan deras* → bukan `strong rain`: **heavy rain**.
- *kopi kental* → bukan `thick coffee` (*thick* untuk sup yang kental atau buku yang tebal): **strong coffee**.
- *harganya mahal* → bukan `the price is expensive`: **the price is high**.
- *masalah berat* → bukan `a heavy problem`: **a serious problem**. *keputusan berat* = **a difficult / tough decision**.

rows.en: The KRL is always crowded at 7 a.m.
rows.id: KRL selalu penuh sesak jam 7 pagi.

rows.en: There's heavy traffic on the toll road to Bandung.
My uncle from Medan has a strong accent.
rows.id: Paman saya dari Medan logatnya kental.
rows.note: a thick or heavy accent is also correct

id.note: a thick atau heavy accent juga benar

rows.en: Hotel prices in Bali are high in December.
rows.id: Harga hotel di Bali mahal di bulan Desember.

rows.en: Choosing a university abroad is a major decision.
rows.id: Memilih universitas di luar negeri adalah keputusan besar.
rows.note: a big decision is also fine

blocks.prompt: Which sentence sounds natural in English?
options: Climate change is a heavy problem for cities on the coast.
Climate change is a serious problem for cities on the coast.
blocks.explain: The partner of problem is serious (or big, major): a serious problem. 'a heavy problem' copies Indonesian masalah berat, but heavy goes with traffic and rain, not problems.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang terdengar alami dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: Pasangan kata problem adalah serious (atau big, major): a serious problem. 'a heavy problem' meniru masalah berat, padahal heavy berpasangan dengan traffic dan rain, bukan problem.

id.title: Kata sifat + kata benda: heavy traffic, strong coffee

material.title: Verb + noun at work: meet a deadline, raise an issue

blocks.text:
At work, many nouns have their own verb. These eight come up in almost every office:
- **meet a deadline** = finish on time (memenuhi tenggat). The opposite: **miss a deadline**. Not `reach the deadline`: you **reach a goal** or a target, but you **meet** a deadline.
- **raise an issue / a question** = bring it up so people discuss it (menyampaikan, mengangkat masalah). Careful: **raise** needs an object (*raise an issue*); **rise** doesn't (*Prices rise every year*).
- **hold a meeting** = organise it (mengadakan rapat). It's a bit formal; *have a meeting* is everyday.
- **set a goal** = decide on a target (menetapkan target). Not `put a goal` (from *pasang target*).
- **make progress** = get better, move forward (ada kemajuan). *progress* is uncountable (it has no plural), so not `a progress` or `progresses`, and not `do progress`.
- **take responsibility for** something (bertanggung jawab atas).
- **run a business / a company / a shop** = manage it (menjalankan usaha).
- **pay attention to** something (memperhatikan).

id.text:
Di kantor, banyak kata benda punya kata kerjanya sendiri. Delapan ini muncul di hampir setiap kantor:
- **meet a deadline** = selesai tepat waktu (memenuhi tenggat). Lawannya: **miss a deadline** (melewati tenggat). Bukan `reach the deadline`: kamu **reach a goal** atau target (mencapai target), tapi deadline itu di-**meet**.
- **raise an issue / a question** = menyampaikan atau mengangkat masalah supaya dibahas. Hati-hati: **raise** butuh objek (*raise an issue*); **rise** tidak (*Prices rise every year* = harga naik setiap tahun).
- **hold a meeting** = mengadakan rapat. Agak formal; *have a meeting* untuk sehari-hari.
- **set a goal** = menetapkan target. Bukan `put a goal` (dari *pasang target*).
- **make progress** = ada kemajuan. *progress* tidak bisa dihitung (tidak punya bentuk jamak), jadi bukan `a progress` atau `progresses`, dan bukan `do progress`.
- **take responsibility for** sesuatu (bertanggung jawab atas).
- **run a business / a company / a shop** = menjalankan usaha, perusahaan, toko.
- **pay attention to** sesuatu (memperhatikan).

blocks.text: Some partners have a close friend that's also correct, so don't worry if you hear it: **bring up** an issue = **raise** an issue; **have** a meeting = **hold** a meeting (less formal); **make the deadline** = **meet the deadline** (informal). But some guesses are always wrong: `reach the deadline`, `do progress`, `put a goal`, `give attention`.

id.text: Beberapa pasangan punya 'teman dekat' yang juga benar, jadi jangan bingung kalau mendengarnya: **bring up** an issue = **raise** an issue; **have** a meeting = **hold** a meeting (kurang formal); **make the deadline** = **meet the deadline** (informal). Tapi beberapa tebakan selalu salah: `reach the deadline`, `do progress`, `put a goal`, `give attention`.

material.title: Adverb + adjective: highly unlikely, fully aware

blocks.text:
Indonesian uses *sangat* or *sekali* with almost every adjective. In English, **very** (or *really, extremely*) is always a safe choice: *very unlikely, very different, very disappointed*. But natural English often uses a **partner adverb**:
- **highly** + likely / unlikely, recommended, successful: *highly unlikely* (kecil sekali kemungkinannya), *highly recommended*, *highly successful*.
- **fully** (= 100%) + aware: *fully aware* (sadar sepenuhnya).
- **deeply** + feelings: *deeply concerned* (sangat prihatin, khawatir), *deeply moved* (sangat terharu).
- **completely** + different, wrong: *completely different* (sama sekali berbeda).
- **bitterly** + disappointed: *bitterly disappointed* (sangat kecewa).

Why not `strongly unlikely`? **strongly** goes with **verbs** of opinion: *I strongly agree, I strongly believe, We strongly recommend it*. It isn't a partner of *unlikely*.

id.text:
Bahasa Indonesia memakai *sangat* atau *sekali* dengan hampir semua kata sifat. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **very** (atau *really, extremely*) selalu pilihan aman: *very unlikely, very different, very disappointed*. Tapi bahasa Inggris yang alami sering memakai **adverb pasangan**:
- **highly** + likely / unlikely, recommended, successful: *highly unlikely* (kecil sekali kemungkinannya), *highly recommended* (sangat direkomendasikan), *highly successful* (sangat sukses).
- **fully** (= 100%) + aware: *fully aware* (sadar sepenuhnya).
- **deeply** + perasaan: *deeply concerned* (sangat prihatin, khawatir), *deeply moved* (sangat terharu).
- **completely** + different, wrong: *completely different* (sama sekali berbeda).
- **bitterly** + disappointed: *bitterly disappointed* (sangat kecewa).

Kenapa bukan `strongly unlikely`? **strongly** berpasangan dengan **kata kerja** pendapat: *I strongly agree* (saya sangat setuju), *I strongly believe*, *We strongly recommend it*. strongly bukan pasangan *unlikely*.

rows.en: This dentist in Bandung is highly recommended.
rows.id: Dokter gigi di Bandung ini sangat direkomendasikan.

rows.en: I'm fully aware that the project is behind schedule.
rows.id: Saya sadar sepenuhnya bahwa proyeknya terlambat dari jadwal.
rows.note: fully + aware (well aware is also fine)

rows.en: Your answer is completely wrong, but the method is good.
rows.id: Jawabanmu salah total, tapi caranya bagus.
rows.note: completely + wrong (totally wrong is also fine)

rows.en: I strongly agree with your plan.

blocks.text: At B2 these are tendencies: often two adverbs are both natural (*deeply / bitterly disappointed*, *completely / totally different*, *fully / well aware*), and **very** is never wrong with them. What sounds strange is the wrong partner: `heavily aware`, `strongly unlikely`, `highly different`. If you're not sure, use **very**, then learn the partner.

id.text: Di B2 ini kecenderungan: sering ada dua adverb yang sama-sama alami (*deeply / bitterly disappointed*, *completely / totally different*, *fully / well aware*), dan **very** tidak pernah salah dengan kata-kata ini. Yang terdengar aneh adalah pasangan yang salah: `heavily aware`, `strongly unlikely`, `highly different`. Kalau ragu, pakai **very**, lalu hafalkan pasangannya.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Bu Ani was ___ disappointed when the client chose another company.
blocks.explain: The partner of disappointed is bitterly (or deeply, very): bitterly disappointed = sangat kecewa. strongly goes with verbs of opinion like agree, not with disappointed.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani was ___ disappointed when the client chose another company.
id.explain: Pasangan disappointed adalah bitterly (atau deeply, very): bitterly disappointed = sangat kecewa. strongly berpasangan dengan kata kerja pendapat seperti agree, bukan dengan disappointed.

id.intro: Hai! Di B1 kamu sudah belajar pasangan untuk make, do, say, tell, have, take dan get. Sekarang kita melangkah lebih jauh: kata sifat dengan kata benda (heavy traffic), kata kerja dengan kata benda di dunia kerja (meet a deadline) dan adverb dengan kata sifat (highly unlikely), supaya bahasa Inggrismu terdengar alami, bukan seperti terjemahan.
